entries.title: Over $4 million drained from DeFiAI
entries.body:
"Our has been hacked and has caused a lot of losses," wrote DeFiAI simply in their announcement. That same day, the project had announced the launch of a new website for their project.

The total funds stolen appear to be around $4.17 million, according to analysis by SlowMist.

entries.title: FTX claims it was hacked as more than $400 million is withdrawn
entries.body:
Over $477 million was mysteriously withdrawn from FTX and FTX US late on November 11, despite the company freezing withdrawals.

An FTX account administrator wrote on the FTX support Telegram, "FTX has been hacked. FTX apps are malware. Delete them. Chat is open. Don't go on FTX site as it might download Trojans". The message was pinned by FTX General Counsel Ryne Miller.

Miller later wrote on Twitter, "Investigating abnormalities with wallet movements related to consolidation of ftx balances across exchanges - unclear facts as other movements not clear. Will share more info as soon as we have it."

A Telegram admin subsequently wrote, "Not all hope is lost. Engineers have managed to retrieve substantial amount of funds," but no details were provided beyond that. A later announcement by Miller claimed that FTX had "initiated precautionary steps to move all digital assets to cold storage", suggesting some of the transfers may have been a part of that effort.

Many speculated that the so-called hack had been coordinated by insiders.

image.alt: Headshot photograph of Bo Shen, wearing a suit
image.caption: Bo Shen

entries.body:
Bo Shen, a general partner at Fenbushi Capital and an early adopter of cryptocurrencies, tweeted on November 22 that two weeks prior, someone had stolen $42 million in cryptocurrencies from his personal wallet. "The stolen assets are personal funds and do not affect on Fenbushi related entities," he wrote.

Analysis by the crypto security firm SlowMist attributed the theft to a compromise of Shen's . Shen had been using the Trust Wallet software, though the theft does not appear to be related to security issues with the wallet software.
entries.title: Early crypto investor loses $42 million in wallet compromise
DFX Finance suffers $5 million loss

image.alt: A circle made of blue-to-turquoise and pink-to-purple gradients, with two notches pointing toward the center, followed by "DFX" in white
image.caption: DFX logo

entries.body: An attacker was able to use a <button class="define-target" id="flash-loan">flash loan</button> to exploit a vulnerability in the <button class="define-target" id="smart-contract">smart contract</button> for DFX Finance, a <button class="define-target" id="defi">decentralized</button> forex trading platform. The platform suffered a loss amounting to around $5 million. The attacker subsequently laundered the funds through the Tornado Cash cryptocurrency <button class="define-target" id="tumbler">tumbler</button>. The attacker didn't make off with the entire amount lost from the platform, partly due to an <button class="define-target" id="mev">MEV</button> bot snagging a significant amount of the funds.

links.linkText: "U.S. Attorney Announces Historic $3.36 Billion Cryptocurrency Seizure And Conviction In Connection With Silk Road Dark Web Fraud"
links.extraText: , U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York

entries.body:
The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York announced that they had convicted James Zhong with wire fraud pertaining to his 2012 theft of around 50,000 Bitcoin from the Silk Road online marketplace. Zhong pled guilty to one count of wire fraud.

The government has filed a motion in the case against Ross Ulbricht, the founder and operator of the Silk Road who is serving life in prison, seeking to retain the seized Bitcoin. At the time of seizure in November 2021, the Bitcoin were notionally worth $3.36 billion. On the date the charges were announced, they would be notionally worth $1.06 billion.
entries.title: U.S. Attorney convicts individual in 2012 theft from the Silk Road, announces seizure of over 50,000 Bitcoin priced at more than $1 billion

entries.title: Pando exploited for $20 million
entries.body: The <button class="define-target" id="defi">defi</button> protocol Pando suffered a $20 million loss when it was exploited with an <button class="define-target" id="oracle-manipulation">oracle manipulation</button> attack. The protocol suspended several of its projects in response to the hack, and wrote that they hoped to negotiate with the hacker to regain some of the stolen proceeds. Some of the stolen funds were able to be <button class="define-target" id="freezing">locked</button>, although it's not clear if it was the total amount.

entries.title: Monkey Drainer steals dozens more NFTs, nets around $867,000
entries.body: The "Monkey Drainer" NFT phishing scammer first identified by blockchain detective zachxbt has struck again. They successfully emptied 7 CryptoPunks and 20 Otherside NFTs, which they flipped for 522 ETH (~$867,000). The scammer then laundered the funds through the Tornado Cash cryptocurrency .

image.alt: "Skyward" in white capitals with a glow effect
image.caption: Skyward Finance logo

entries.body:
Skyward Finance is a project based on the NEAR blockchain, aiming to help users with initial token distribution. The project's treasury was drained of 1.1 million NEAR (~$3.2 million) after a hacker discovered a vulnerability in the project's . Crypto exploit research group Rekt wrote, "The fact that it took over a year for anyone to find this relatively simple exploit is remarkable." and questioned, "Was this incident an honest, albeit simple, mistake? Or a planned ejector seat?"

The project was unusually frank in their announcement, writing on Twitter that the hack had "render[ed] the Treasury and the $SKYWARD token effectively worthless... We recommend users to withdraw their funds safely where they can and for the community to no longer interact with Skyward."
entries.title: Skyward Finance treasury drained of $3.2 million

image.alt: Solend logo: Two interlocking S's in orange, followed by "Solend" in white
image.caption: Solend logo

entries.body: Solend announced that an exploiter had manipulated the oracle price of an asset on their platform, allowing them to take out a loan that left the platform with $1.26 million in <button class="define-target" id="bad-debt">bad debt</button>. They reported that they had paused affected pools, and did not anticipate other pools on the platform were at risk.
entries.title: Oracle attack on Solend costs the project $1.26 million

image.alt: A green outline of a cube, followed by "Rubic" in white
image.caption: Rubic logo

entries.body:
An attacker was able to compromise the private key of an admin wallet for the Rubic crypto exchange, transferring around 34 million Rubic tokens. The attacker then sold the tokens on decentralized exchanges Uniswap and PancakeSwap.

The enormous sale caused the token price to plummet from $0.082 to $0.016, an 80% decrease. The stolen tokens were nominally worth almost $2.8 million (priced at the value before the theft), but it's not likely the attackers were able to exchange them for that much given the lack of liquidity to absorb such a huge sale.
entries.title: Rubic exchange private key compromised, token plummets
